items.reason: The comment includes the shared pool lifecycle bug: closing one strategy shuts down the factory-owned pool used by other strategies. Giving each strategy its own pool addresses the golden issue as well.
The shutdown flag makes workers exit before draining queued items. This is the same graceful-shutdown defect described in the golden issue.

This alleges CPU usage proportional to the numeric offset gap, rather than either golden offset-correctness problem. The claim is false: the loop breaks at the first missing offset instead of traversing the gap.
